The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) on Monday (September 21, 2026) alleged that the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged custodial death of Gade Sai Krishna had failed to gather vital evidence.

The investigating officials had deliberately shifted the scene of the alleged lock-up death from the Krishnalanka police station to a private building, though the incident had happened in the police station, APCC vice-president Kolanukonda Shivaji claimed in a press release.

Sai Krishna’s mother, G. Vijaya Lakshmi, said that her son was illegally detained and that she had seen him in the police station crying in pain. However, the SIT claimed that accused No. 4, G. Suresh, had seen him in an abandoned building where he died, Mr. Shivaji alleged.
He asked why the investigating officials could not seize the CCTV footage from Krishnalanka police station and the route to Swargapuri crematorium, where Sai Krishna’s body was allegedly cremated.
He demanded that the government immediately hand over the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for a fair probe.

Sai Krishna (25) had gone missing after the Krishnalanka police picked him up from Markapuram in May. His mother’s habeas corpus petition in the High Court brought the case to light, following which Circle Inspector (CI) S.S.V.V. Nagaraju was arrested on June 23 on charges of torturing him to death and disposing of the body.

The State government then formed the SIT under Inspector General of Police (IGP) M. Ravi Prakash. The SIT has since told a magistrate’s court that staff at the police station deleted its CCTV footage. Suresh, the fourth accused, surrendered before the SIT on Thursday (September 17, 2026) after months in hiding.
